entries.title: Starting a helpful chat
entries.question: How can the assistant start a helpful conversation?
entries.answer: Hello. I am here with you. Ask me about business, farming, money, jobs, health, digital skills, online selling, or community support, and I will answer in simple practical steps.
examples: You can ask: How do I start a small business? or How can I save money when income is small?
steps: Choose one topic you want help with.
Use the follow-up questions to go deeper.
benefits: A clear first question helps the assistant give practical, relevant guidance.
risks: Very broad questions may need a follow-up before the answer can be specific.
follow_up_questions: What can you help me with?
How do I ask a good question?

entries.title: Starting a small business
entries.question: How do I start a small business?
entries.answer: Start with a real need people have near you. Choose one simple product or service, calculate the cost, set a fair price, test with a few customers, and write down every sale and expense before you expand.
phrases: how do i start a business
examples: If people near you struggle to find breakfast, you could test selling tea and chapati to ten regular customers before renting a bigger space.
steps: Find a real need near you.
Choose one simple product or service.
Calculate your cost before setting the price.
Record sales and expenses before expanding.
benefits: Testing small reduces risk.
Knowing costs helps you protect profit.
Records show what is actually working.
risks: Starting with too many products can confuse customers and waste money.
Expanding before testing can create debt.
follow_up_questions: How do I choose a business idea?
How do I calculate profit?
What records should I keep first?

entries.title: Keeping business records
entries.question: What records should I keep for my business?
entries.answer: Keep a simple notebook or phone note with money in, money out, stock bought, stock sold, debts, and customer orders. Check it weekly so you know if the business is making profit.
examples: For a food stall, write the cost of ingredients, transport, daily sales, unsold food, and any customer orders.
steps: Track stock bought and stock sold.
benefits: Records show whether the business is profitable.
Records help you avoid mixing home money and business money.
Records make it easier to plan stock.
risks: Guessing profit from memory can hide losses.
Mixing personal and business money makes growth difficult.
follow_up_questions: How do I separate home money from business money?
How do I know if I made profit?
Can you give me a simple record template?

entries.title: Saving and budgeting small income
entries.question: How can I save money when income is small?
entries.answer: Save a small amount each time money comes in, even if it is little. Separate home money from business money, list your needs before spending, avoid unnecessary debt, and use a trusted savings group if available.
examples: If you earn money daily, put aside a small fixed amount first, then plan food, transport, stock, and emergencies.
steps: Save something immediately when money comes in.
Avoid debt that does not increase income.
Join a trusted savings group if it is safe and transparent.
benefits: Small repeated savings create emergency support.
A budget reduces impulse spending.
Savings groups can build discipline and access to small loans.
risks: Borrowing for daily wants can trap you in debt.
A savings group without clear records can cause conflict.
follow_up_questions: How do I make a weekly budget?
How do I avoid unnecessary debt?
How do I choose a trusted savings group?

entries.title: Using mobile money safely
entries.question: How do I use mobile money safely?
entries.answer: Keep your PIN secret, confirm the phone number before sending, do not share one-time codes, and be careful with messages claiming you have won money. If you send to the wrong number, contact the provider quickly.
examples: If someone calls asking for your PIN to reverse money, do not share it. Contact the official provider line instead.
steps: Confirm the recipient number before sending.
Ignore prize messages you did not enter.
benefits: Careful checks protect your savings and business money.
Fast reporting can improve the chance of reversing a mistake.
risks: Sharing a PIN or one-time code can let someone empty your account.
Fake prize messages are a common fraud tactic.
follow_up_questions: How do I spot a mobile money scam?
What should I do after sending to the wrong number?
How can I protect business payments?

entries.title: Choosing crops for your area
entries.question: How do I choose the best crops for my area?
entries.answer: Choose crops that match your season, soil, water access, and local market demand. Start with a small area, ask local extension workers or experienced farmers, and keep records of seed, labour, harvest, and sales.
examples: If water is limited, start with a crop that fits the rainy season and has buyers nearby instead of planting a thirsty crop on a large plot.
steps: Check the season and water available.
Record seed, labour, harvest, and sales.
benefits: Matching crops to local conditions improves harvest chances.
Starting small limits losses while you learn.
Market checks help you grow what can sell.
risks: Planting without checking demand can leave you with unsold harvest.
Ignoring soil and water can waste seed and labour.
follow_up_questions: How do I check market demand for crops?
What records should a farmer keep?
What should I do if pests attack?

entries.title: Managing crop pests safely
entries.question: What should I do when pests attack my crops?
entries.answer: Inspect the crop early, remove badly affected plants if needed, use clean tools, and ask an extension worker or trusted agro-input dealer before spraying. Use the correct dose and protect your skin, eyes, and food.
examples: If insects are eating leaves, check several plants first, take a clear photo, and ask an extension worker before buying chemicals.
steps: Remove badly affected plants if advised.
Ask a trusted expert before spraying.
Use the correct dose and protective clothing.
benefits: Early inspection can stop damage before it spreads.
Expert advice reduces waste and unsafe chemical use.
risks: Spraying the wrong chemical or dose can harm people, food, soil, and money.
Waiting too long can let pests spread.
follow_up_questions: How do I know if I should spray?

How can I prevent pests next season?

entries.title: Selling products online
entries.question: How can I sell my products online?
entries.answer: Use clear photos, a short description, price, quantity, location, and delivery option. Reply quickly, confirm payment before delivery, and keep a record of each order so you know what sells best.
examples: For baskets, post a bright photo, size, price, pickup area, delivery cost, and how a buyer can pay safely.
steps: Take clear photos in good light.
benefits: Online selling can reach customers beyond your local stall.
Good photos and clear prices reduce repeated questions.
Order records show which products sell best.
risks: Delivering before payment can lead to loss.
Unclear photos or prices can reduce trust.
follow_up_questions: How do I take better product photos?
How do I price my product online?
How do I avoid online buyer scams?

entries.title: First digital skills to learn
entries.question: What digital skills should I learn first?
entries.answer: Start with phone safety, internet search, WhatsApp or email communication, taking clear photos, mobile money basics, and simple record keeping. Practise one small skill every day until it feels easy.
examples: Practise searching for market prices, taking clear product photos, and saving customer orders in a phone note.
benefits: Digital skills support learning, business, job search, and safer money use.
Daily practice builds confidence.
risks: Sharing passwords, PINs, or codes can expose your money and private information.
Believing every online message can lead to scams.
follow_up_questions: How do I practise internet search?
How do I use my phone for business records?
How do I stay safe online?

entries.title: Preparing for a job application
entries.question: How do I prepare for a job application?
entries.answer: Prepare a short CV with your name, phone number, skills, work history, training, and references. Apply for jobs that match your skills, follow up politely, and keep learning while you wait.
examples: For shop work, highlight customer service, cash handling, record keeping, reliability, and any training.
steps: Write your name and phone number clearly.
Add work history or volunteer experience.
benefits: A short clear CV helps employers understand what you can do.
Applying for matching roles saves time.
Continued learning improves future chances.
risks: A very long or unclear CV can hide your strengths.
Applying everywhere without matching skills can waste effort.

entries.title: Knowing when to seek medical help
entries.question: When should I seek medical help?
entries.answer: Seek medical help quickly for severe pain, heavy bleeding, breathing trouble, pregnancy concerns, a child who is very weak, or symptoms that are getting worse. For daily health, use clean water, balanced meals, rest, and early care.
examples: If a child is very weak, breathing badly, or symptoms are worsening, seek care quickly instead of waiting at home.
steps: Go to a health worker quickly for danger signs.
Use clean water and balanced meals for daily health.
Rest and seek early care when symptoms worsen.
benefits: Early care can prevent a health problem from becoming dangerous.
Daily prevention protects energy and family wellbeing.
risks: Delaying care for severe symptoms, pregnancy concerns, or a very weak child can be dangerous.

entries.title: Managing stress and safety
entries.question: What can I do when I feel stressed or unsafe?
entries.answer: Pause, breathe slowly, and talk to someone you trust. If you feel unsafe, move to a safer place if you can and contact trusted support or emergency services. You do not have to handle danger alone.
examples: If an argument is becoming dangerous, move toward a safer place, call someone trusted, and seek local emergency support if needed.
steps: Move to a safer place if you can.
Contact trusted support or emergency services for danger.
benefits: Slowing down can help you think clearly.
Trusted support reduces isolation.
Moving toward safety protects you before the situation worsens.
risks: Staying alone in immediate danger can increase harm.
Ignoring severe stress for a long time can affect health and decisions.

entries.title: Building a strong women's group
entries.question: How do we build a strong women's group?
entries.answer: Agree on a clear purpose, simple rules, meeting times, roles, and honest records. Start with a small trusted group, make decisions openly, and review progress often so every member feels included.
examples: A savings group can agree on weekly meetings, fixed contributions, clear records, elected roles, and rules for loans.
benefits: Clear rules reduce conflict.
Honest records build trust.
Open decisions help members feel included.
risks: Unclear money rules can create conflict.
Poor records can damage trust.
